To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a synthetic co-cultivate of C. autoetanogenum and C. kluyvri, can produce a higher yield of chain elongation acids from CO, by driving the metabolism of the C. autoethanoegenum towards solventogenesis.

a co-culture of C. autoetanogenum and C. kluyferi, in which C. kluyfervi is the sole ethanol consumer, drives the metabolic flux of the former towards ethanol formation, resulting in a higher yield of chain elongation products from carbon monoxides.

a co-culture of C. autoetanogenum and C. kluyvéri can produce high amounts of chain elongated compounds from carbon monoxide, and that the production of these compounds is enhanced when the co-culture is supplemented with ethanol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of synthetic microbial consortia for the sustainable production of chemicals.
the design of synthetic co-cultures to promote the production of chain elongated compounds from CO.
the development of sustainable production processes for chemicals and fuels.

the co-culture of C. autothanoegenum and C. kluyvri results in an improved production process for chain elongated products.

the co-cultivation of C. auto and C. kluy resulted in a shift in the metabolic pathway of C. auto from ethanol production to acetone-butanol-ethanol production, resulting in a 1.6-fold increase in the production of C4- and C5-carbon chains from CO-derived electrons.

co-cultivation of C. autoetnhanogenum and C. kluyvei results in a metabolic shift in C. autoetanogenum towards ethanol production, resulting in an increase in the yield of chain elongation products from carbon monoxides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the thermodynamic interaction of two microbes can be used to promote the desired production of chain elongation acids from syngus.

the thermodynamics of the co-cultivation of C. autoetanogenum and C. kluyferi is such that C. autoetnogenum produces ethanol and the co-culture produces a high yield of C6-C10 alcohols and fatty acids.
the co-cultivation strategy can be a promising alternative to genetic engineering for improving bio-catalytic processes.

the microbial interactions between C. autoethano-genum and C. kluy-very are governed by the thermodynamic interactions.
the metabolic shift in C. autoethenagenum is driven by thermodynamics.
